## Follow-up: point 3 tested

I ran the specs locally on this branch (JDK 25): `AnnotationMemberDefaultsSpec` (3/3) and `NestedAnnotationDefaultsSpec` (1/1) pass.

To check point 3, I added a scratch spec in the same style as the new test. A Java annotation with these two defaults is added by a visitor, and its defaults are read once with no source using it and once with a source using it:

```java
Class<?> arrayClass() default String[].class;
Class<?> primitiveClass() default int.class;
```

The two compilations disagree:

| Default | No usage (compiled class) | With a usage (KSP) |
|---|---|---|
| `String[].class` | `[Ljava.lang.String;` | `java.lang.Object[]` |
| `int.class` | `int` | `java.lang.Integer` |

So for annotations with array-class or primitive-class defaults, an incremental build and a clean build can still produce different defaults, which is the difference this PR sets out to remove. The open point about a primitive `KClass` default is real, and array classes are affected too.

The KSP side is arguably the less accurate one: it drops the element type and boxes the primitive. Either way, the new path should produce whatever the usage path produces, or both should be fixed together. It's probably also worth adding these two defaults to `AddedDefaults`.

Point 1 (a member missing from the class on the processor path is skipped, and the partial defaults are cached) I confirmed by reading the code only.
